A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments on Friedman 1, Ishigami and G-function data, plus UK Biobank proteomic analyses of BMI.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds PFI experiments, controlled breast-cancer gene recovery, a high-dimensional simulation, TabICL evaluation and ranking-stability results.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains computing importance on an ensemble that averages predictions, using bagging or voting. The added importance-method analyses and base learners do not introduce a new aggregation algorithm or modify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds TCGA BRCA four-class subtype classification with 572 patients and 50 genes, including 40 permuted control genes. Appendix H also adds a distinct nonlinear simulation with 100 features and 25 relevant variables, substantially extending task and data coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison remains ensemble-level importance versus averaged individual-model importances. Logistic regression, TabICL and PFI extend the base-learner or importance-measure settings; they are not additional competing aggregation methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include stratified 10-fold classification with cross-entropy LOCO and top-K gene recovery, a two-layer 256-unit MLP simulation with ground truth estimated at 10,000 samples, and TabICL ensembles. Appendix J adds average pairwise Spearman correlation across folds as an evaluation metric. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices H-I test whether the advantage persists with higher dimensionality, larger support and a foundation model. Appendix J directly examines ranking stability across data splits. These extend the retained bagging-versus-voting, support-versus-null-feature and bias-variance analyses.

E5.justification: The new TCGA experiment specifies repetition across 10 random seeds and standard-deviation bands for recovery curves. Existing 100-seed synthetic reporting, bootstrap intervals and five-fold UK Biobank uncertainty remain unchanged; this does not establish increased repetition of existing experiments.

E6.justification: Original plotted results are retained. New Figures 11 and 16-19 report little PFI benefit, improved controlled driver-gene recovery, lower importance MSE in the 100-feature and TabICL settings, and greater ranking stability. TabICL feature-selection AUC is near ceiling for both strategies. These are additional results under new settings, not revised scores for the original experiments.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix D add a PFI error analysis invoking support positivity and claiming quadratic-error cancellation. Appendix E defines Integrated Gradients and derives exact equivalence between the two aggregation strategies. Appendix A.1 also changes the remainder sign from -r_n to +r_n; the original LOCO and SAGE theorems are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and two principal contribution statements remain unchanged. The introduction broadens the stated analytical scope to PFI and Integrated Gradients, while the discussion explicitly qualifies the recommendation by importance method and rejects a single theorem covering every method.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for weak PFI gains and exact Integrated Gradients equivalence, extending the applicability discussion. The existing tabular-data limitation remains, but its statement that permutation and gradient methods are excluded now conflicts with the added analyses.

D1.justification: v1 describes supplementary code and promises a future public release; v2 reports public availability and supplies a repository link in Section 5. New appendices document gene permutation, ensemble configurations, the larger MLP and ground-truth estimation settings. Existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Catav et al. (2021) and Janssen et al. (2023) for the biological benchmark protocol, and Qu et al. (2025) for TabICL. It also acknowledges prior aggregation research more explicitly and softens the claimed absence of a stability definition to a lack of consensus.

P1.justification: Localized introduction edits, an expanded discussion and additional appendix sections preserve most original prose and the main narrative. v2 also adds acknowledgements and an impact statement, relocates code availability, and replaces the placeholder conference header.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial visual evidence through PFI comparison plots, biological recovery panels, high-dimensional and TabICL results, and a multi-panel stability figure. All original figures are retained, with some relocated or renumbered; the original CFI plots are now separated across pages under Appendix E.1.

improvement.justification: Appendices G-J strengthen validation through controlled biological recovery, broader model/data settings and direct ranking-stability measurement, while the repository link improves reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by the new PFI derivation: support positivity does not make marginally permuted and original input distributions identical, so its asserted quadratic-error cancellation is not established. The unchanged limitations also contradict the added PFI/IG coverage. The retained central recommendation is better supported, but the expansion introduces unresolved theoretical and scope inconsistencies.
